title: Shore up prefetch fallback and tenant isolation to stop cross-host queue starvation
creator: Aisha Patel
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket opened after two priority customer escalations (Cust-A, Cust-B) reporting recurring 95th/99th token-latency spikes on Dedicated clusters during mixed short+long-context waves.

2026-03-10: Initial triage by oncall (Samir Gupta) identified correlation with prefetch handoff churn and host-level admission exhaustion when long-context KV handoffs coincide with microbursts of short requests.

2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with stress harness (mixed-length generator) and validated queue-starvation scenario when prefetch threads create transient inflight reservations leading to admission blackout for short flows.

2026-03-11: Temporary mitigation deployed to Hosted region us-west: reduce prefetch concurrency by 30% and enable admission-grace-window; immediate customer latency improvement observed for Cust-A (99th down from 2.4s to 480ms).

2026-03-12: Engineering design review: decided to implement a two-part fix — (1) prefetch quarantine (timebound prefetched KV entries that can't be immediately admitted) and (2) a fallback admission path that allows high-priority short requests to bypass long-context handoffs when queue depth > threshold.

2026-03-12: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive eviction vs. graceful quarantine. Chosen quarantine to avoid cache thrashing observed in earlier incidents; quarantine keeps KV so long-requests don't repeatedly reload from storage but prevents inflight reservation leakage.

2026-03-13: Implemented prototype that adds per-tenant quarantine buckets and a lightweight preemption token for short-request fast-path. Unit tests and new integration tests added to runtime test-suite.
2026-03-13: PR opened: runtime#4123 (link above). Requesting reviews from storage (Elena Morozova) and scheduler (Claire Zhang).

2026-03-14: Canary rollout plan approved by SRE. Metrics to watch: short-request QPS, 95/99 token latency, prefetch-quarantine occupancy, kv-cache hit ratio, and admission-skip rate. Initial canary targeted to 5% of Hosted traffic and one Dedicated customer cluster with low risk.

2026-03-14: Noted follow-ups: add tenant-level throttles to avoid starvation in edge cases (follow-up ticket), and expand chaos tests to simulate cross-host prefetch collisions under maintenance windows.
acceptance_criteria: Canary shows at least 50% reduction in 99th token latency for mixed short+long workloads compared to prefix baseline
No increase >3% in overall token cost after quarantine enabled (justify with telemetry)
No regression in KV-cache hit ratio beyond acceptable margin (<=5% drop), scoped by release tests
Automated integration test reproducing the original starvation pattern passes in CI
Operational playbook updated with rollback steps and monitoring runbook entries
test_plan: Unit tests for quarantine lifecycle (enqueue, timebound release, eviction)
Integration test: mixed-length stress harness (10k short reqs/sec + long context streams) validated pre/post fix for 95/99 metrics
Chaos test: simulate host maintenance & prefetch collisions across 3 hosts to verify no cross-host admission collapse
Load test on Dedicated staging cluster with customer-like request mix (mirror Cust-B production trace)
Telemetry assertions in CI that fail the build if quorum metrics deviate beyond thresholds
rollout_plan: Step 1 (Canary): Deploy runtime-1.23.0 with feature flag prefetch_quarantine=on to 5% Hosted capacity + selected Dedicated staging cluster (24h observation)
Step 2 (Observe): Monitor dashboards for 99th token latency, kv hit ratio, quarantine occupancy, and admission-skip rate. Hold if 99th regresses >10% or error rate increases >0.5%
Step 3 (Gradual): If canary stable, increment to 25% for 12h, then 60% for 6h, then full rollout. Target Dedicated rollout only after Hosted reaches 60%
Step 4 (Customer opt-in): For Private deployments, provide patch and runbook; coordinate with account engineering for on-prem upgrades
Rollback criteria: any sustained increase in service errors (>0.5% for 30m) or persistent 99th latency regression (>10% for 30m) triggers immediate rollback to previous runtime and feature flag off
